full_judgment:
M Enayetur Rahim, J: By filing this application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh the petitioner has challenged the Notice as contained in Memo No. 44565 dated 6-11-2016 (Annexure-A) issued by the Respondent No. 2 purportedly under section 26 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 (hereinafter referred to as Act of 2004).

2. In the application it is contended that the petitioner, an Ex-Chairman of Ekushey Television Ltd. while is in detention in central jail, Dhaka in connection with some criminal cases, on 16-10-2016 a notice under section 26(1) of the Act of 2004 bearing memo No. 44565 along with a form under rule 17(2) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007 was issued under the signature of Respondent No. 2 directing him to submit statement of all moveable and immovable properties in his name and in benami, liabilities, source of income and detailed statement within 7 (seven) days of receipt of the said notice, since the Respondent No. 1, Anti-Corruption Commission on the basis of receipt of information and enquiry reached firm belief that the petitioner had amassed huge amount of wealth and property in his name and in benami and owning the same, which is beyond his known source of income. The jail authority served the notice upon the petitioner on 5-2-2016.

3. Being aggrieved by the said notice the petitioner has filed this application.

4. Mr. Moynul Hossain, the learned Advocate, appearing with Mr. Jahedul Islam, the learned Advocate, for the writ petitioner submits that the impugned notice is without lawful authority and is of no legal effect as the same being served upon a detenue who has no way to access his papers so as to give accurate reply to the same failing which he faces threat of three years imprisonment is a nullity and not a notice contemplated under section 26 of the Act of 2004.

5. In this connection Mr. Hossain referred to the case of Anti-Corruption Commission vs Dr. Mohiuddin Khan Alamgir, reported in 62 DLR (AD) 290.

6. He further submits that along with the notice the Anti-Corruption Commission ought to have furnished the report of the inquiry on the basis of which the notice was issued and the petitioner has a right to get the said report of inquiry to give proper reply of the impugned notice.

7. We have also heard Mr. Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned Advocate for the Respondent No. 1.

8. Heard the learned Advocate for the parties, perused the impugned notice and other materials annexured to the application.

9. In the case of Moudud Ahmed vs. State (heard along with four other Appeals), reported in 68 DLR (AD) 118 Appellate Division has reviewed some of the observations made in the case of Anti-Corruption Commission vs. Mohiuddin Khan Alamgir, reported in 62 DLR (AD) 290.

10. In the above case Appellate Division has observed to the effect:

"In the case reported in 62 DLR (AD) 290 the learned Advocate for the ACC failed to make proper submissions in respect of the issues involved in the case. Because of the learned Advocate's failure to make correct sub-missions in assisting the court properly at the time of hearing of the leave petition this Division made some passing observations by the way in paragraph Nos. 44 and 45, in the absence of argument, without reference to the relevant provisions of law, which have no relevance or bearing in the disposal of the case and those observations have not arisen in such a manner as to require a decision in the disposal of the matter. Even some of the observations in paragraph Nos. 44 and 45 do not reflect the correct principle of law in view of the discussions made and decisions cited herein above and all these observations made in paragraph Nos. 44 and 45 are obiter dictum and some of the observations do not depict the correct principle of law and cannot be justified by the relevant provisions of law"

And

"In the instant case there is no difficulty in reviewing the decision of this Division in the case reported in 62 DLR (AD) 290 and passing necessary order with regard to the aforesaid observations made in paragraph Nos. 44 and 45 of the judgment and order of this Division passed in the Criminal Petition for leave Appeal No. 398 of 2009."

<u>11. In the above case the Appellate Division has held that if the notice is served upon a detenue by the Commission is valid one and on the plea of detention there is no scope to say that the Commission has no authority (to serve a notice upon a detenue.</u>

12. In the impugned notice it has been categorically mentioned that;

“যেহেতু প্রাপ্ত তথ্যের ভিত্তিতে অনুসন্ধান করিয়া দুর্নীতি দমন কমিশনের স্থির বিশ্বাস জন্মিয়াছে যে, আপনি জনাব আব্দুস সালাম, সাবেক চেয়ারম্যান, একুশে টেলিভিশন লিঃ, পিতা-মৃত এম এ করিম, বর্তমান ঠিকানা হাউজ নং-৩৩৬, রোড নং-২৩, নিউ ডিওএইচএস, মহাখালী, ঢাকা-১২১২। জ্ঞাত আয়ের বর্হির্ভূত স্বনামে/বেনামে বিপুল পরিমাণ সম্পদ/সম্পত্তির মালিক হইয়াছেন।”

<u>13. In view of the above assertions made by the Commission there is no scope to say that the Commission being a statutory body issued the notice without applying its judicial mind and mechanically having no materials before it. Further, ‘স্থির বিশ্বাস’ in other word satisfaction of the Commission cannot be challenged and decided invoking Article 102 of the Constitution.</u>

14. In case of Moudud Ahmed vs. State, Appellate Division also observed to the effect:

"Therefore, there is no difficulty to say that before issuance of any notice under section 26 of the ACC Act upon a person the Commission must have knowledge that the said person has acquired property beyond known source of income. In other words, the fact of acquiring property beyond some one's known source of income was within the knowledge of the Commission long before the issuance of the order/notice under section 26 of the Act."

15. In the case of ACC vs. Sheikh Hasina, reported in 60 DLR (AD) 172 (paragraph-32) the Appellate Division held as under:

"Moreover, the Commission was not required to disclose any specific material or investigation report for issuing an order asking for statement of assets and the satisfaction is that of the Commission and none else as has been held in the case of Mustafizur Rahman vs DG Anti-Corruption Commission, reported in 49 DLR, 599. So, the objective satisfaction is not contemplated by the Act."

<u>16. In the case of Mustafizur Rahman and 3 others vs. DG, Anti-Corruption, 49 DLR 599 it has been held by a Division Bench of the High Division that the Bureau of Anti-Corruption is not required to disclose specific material or investigation report to the petitioner in the notice requiring submission of statement of income and assets (paragraph 31).</u>

17. Having considered as above we do not find any merit in the application. And the same is misconceived one.

Accordingly, the application is rejected summarily.

End.
